These uts failed because of invalid finalizer name. I'll fix that after reviewers confirm that this is the right way to go.

> Although documented, this might have impact on the ecosystem.

Exactly this. This is not a backwards compatible change, and would impact some callers who are currently working just fine. There's no security reason to break compatibility, and we typically only tighten validation in cases which were not previously working at all (to make API validation catch what would lead to a failure at runtime).

We would *prefer* people use domain-qualified finalizers to avoid conflicts with other uncoordinated controllers, but I think we'd limit this to a warning, not make it an error. To do that, we would detect use of unqualified finalizers in customResourceStrategy#WarningsOnCreate and customResourceStrategy#WarningsOnUpdate and just warn, rather than fail validation

> we would detect use of unqualified finalizers in customResourceStrategy#WarningsOnCreate and customResourceStrategy#WarningsOnUpdate and just warn, rather than fail validation

Got it. I think it's better to do it in `customResourceValidator`#WarningsOnUpdate and `customResourceValidator`#WarningsOnCreate but not `customResourceStrategy`.

issue_context.title: api: Finalizer name format is not enforced for custom resources
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

A client is allowed to add custom finalizers to Custom Resources with a finalizer name that's not fully qualified (e.g. `example` or `example.com`).

However they're prevented from doing the same on builtin resource types, returning the following error:

    Invalid value: "finalizers.compute.linkedin.com": name is neither a standard finalizer name nor is it fully qualified

### What did you expect to happen?

Per [Custom Resource Definition docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#finalizers:~:text=Identifiers%20of%20custom%20finalizers%20consist%20of%20a%20domain%20name%2C%20a%20forward%20slash%20and%20the%20name%20of%20the%20finalizer), custom finalizer names are expected to be in format "consist of a domain name, a forward slash and the name of the finalizer" (e.g. `foo.bar/name`).

Therefore, I expected the enforcement to be the same for CRs and builtin types.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. have a custom resource on the cluster
2. `kubectl edit` it to add `finalizers: [example.com]`
3. observe the edit does not fail
4. do the same on a builtin resource (e.g. Namespace or Pod), observe it fails

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

Reproducible at least starting from 1.21 and still on latest versions.
